svg.title: The invisible leak, worked out — how $40-75K a year walks away
svg.desc: A mid-size hotel laundry processing 5,000 pieces a day loses 8-12 percent of textile inventory yearly through four quiet exits: miscounting, misrouting, ward hoarding and premature disposal. The arithmetic: a 50,000-piece par level at a 10 percent loss rate, with replacement at $8-15 per piece, drains $40,000-75,000 every year — and manual counting, itself 3-5 percent inaccurate, cannot even see the leak, so operations buy more stock to cover it.
svg.text: Four quiet exits, one loud annual number

g.text: miscounted — tallies drift 3–5% even with diligent staff
misrouted — delivered to the wrong customer, never mentioned
hoarded — squirrelled away on wards and floors
discarded — thrown out while still perfectly serviceable

svg.text: 8–12% of inventory gone yearly · at 10% loss on 50,000 pieces:
And because manual counts can't see the leak, procurement buys extra stock to cover it —
the equivalent of fixing a slow leak by buying more buckets.
The losses stay invisible until the annual count. Item-level tracking makes them visible on Tuesday.
